The forward problem is described by the time-harmonic Maxwell equations with the goal of reconstructing the refractive index of an inhomogeneous medium.
The inverse problem is highly ill-conditioned, requiring regularization techniques to handle data noise.
The paper proposes using spectral preconditioning based on the Lanczos method to efficiently solve the regularized Newton equations.
Updating the spectral preconditioner during the Newton iterations is shown to improve performance, especially at high accuracy levels.
The Lepskii-type stopping rule outperforms the commonly used discrepancy principle, providing more accurate reconstructions in the presence of random noise.
The paper uses between 98,304 and 786,432 degrees of freedom to represent the electric field for each incident wave direction and polarization.
The unknown refractive index perturbation is represented using 500 to 2000 coefficients of tensor products of splines and spherical harmonics.
The paper uses 25 incident waves with random directions and polarizations to generate the 5,000-dimensional data vector.
For exact data, the IRGNM with updated preconditioning outperforms other iterative regularization methods in terms of work-precision diagrams.
In the presence of 2% relative noise, the Lepskii-type stopping rule achieves a mean L2 error of 0.0474, compared to 0.0744 for the discrepancy principle.
The discrepancy principle is shown to stop the iteration too early, with (||F(xk) - y|| << ||ε||) at the optimal stopping index.
The paper demonstrates the importance of accurately approximating the largest isolated eigenvalues of the Jacobian for effective spectral preconditioning.
Updating the preconditioner is found to be necessary as the regularization parameter γ tends to zero during the Newton iterations.
The Lanczos method is used to approximate the eigenpairs of the preconditioned Jacobian, exploiting its close connection to the preconditioned conjugate gradient method.

The paper provides a convergence analysis of the IRGNM in combination with the discrepancy principle, but notes that the required conditions have not been verified for the electromagnetic medium scattering problem.
